summary: Third lighthouse of Ashtabula harbor, a steel-plated house on a breakwater crib that was moved in 1915-16, iced solid in January 1928 and manned until 1973.

access.note: Half a mile offshore on a breakwater; reached by boat; tours by appointment through the owning society, weather permitting.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: first keeper of 1836 light (Miniger vs Bigelow); year of the move (Aug 1915 per Lighthouse Friends vs commissioning 21 Sept 1916 per Commissioner); keeper quarters 1896 (USLHS) vs 1898 addition (LHF); Society's keeper list (Walworth to 1905, Anderson to 1915) vs NARA-based roster. NRHP nomination text not digitised (NPGallery placeholder), so NRHP info is the NPGallery metadata only. No newspaper evidence: loc.gov searches via newspapers.py timed out. Efficiency-flag table (1921 Bulletin) read by column position: Scobie matched to Ashtabula, 10th district; verify. Lighthouse Friends gives 'about 1,750 ft' and the Commissioner 'about 1,800 ft'; 1930s breakwater extension of 600 ft (LHF) not used in the story. Roster is the USLHS list unaltered; 'Willliam H. Field' spelled as printed; LHF spells Wasilowski vs USLHS Wasiloswki. Station kind: record's first_lit 1836 is the harbour's first light, not this structure; consider first_lit 1905. The Great Lakes Lighthouse Historian blog page conflicts with other sources and was not used. Fixed in verification: footnote 4 is the Light-House Board report for fiscal 1891 (the 1892 report starts at scan p. 326 of that volume). The ship name 'Harry Yates' is OCR-damaged in the 1928 Bulletin ('Han''Y Yo.tes'); it matches the known Great Lakes freighter Harry Yates (built 1910). The efficiency-flag row is matched on one OCR line and the 1918-23 Bulletin index also lists 'Scobie, R.H.B., keeper Ashtabula, efficiency flag awarded'.
